title: DOJ Issues Grand Jury Subpoena to James Comey Confidant Daniel Richman
partialText: The subpoena of Daniel C. Richman is the latest move in a persistent campaign to go after James B. Comey, one of President Trump’s most reviled political adversaries who has already been indicted twice.

title: IRS Audit Revenue Has Plummeted Under Trump, Watchdog Finds
partialText: The I.R.S. lost roughly a quarter of its employees since President Trump took office, hampering the agency’s ability to conduct audits.

title: Summit With Russia, India and Iran Shows Leverage Wars Have Given Xi of China
partialText: A two-day conference of the 10-nation Shanghai Cooperation Organization in Kyrgyzstan shows the limits of U.S. economic warfare.

title: Europe Protests as U.S. Invites Russian Minister to G20 Finance Meeting
partialText: The meeting, which China and Russia are attending, is focused on the ongoing economic shock from the war in Iran, which has driven up oil prices globally.

title: FTC and 22 States Sue Amazon Over Advertising Practices
partialText: Regulators say the e-commerce giant forced millions of advertisers to pay more than they should have. The company denies the claims.

title: These Generals Fought for Israel. Now They See ‘Jewish Terrorism’ as the Threat.
partialText: A growing number of former Israeli generals, intelligence officials and prime ministers are accusing settlers in the West Bank of committing ethnic cleansing with government support. “Once a society behaves this way,” one said, “that society is doomed.”

title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields: A New Feminist Music Festival Takes Shape
partialText: At the first Daisy Chain Fields festival, the 23-year-old pop star presented a cross-generational vision of female empowerment. (With Taco Bell activations, too.)

title: Study A.I. Consciousness? The Bots Would Like a Word With You.
partialText: Given access to email, A.I. agents have started reaching out to the philosophers and researchers exploring deep questions about them.

title: Pennsylvania’s A.I. Gold Rush Meets Second Thoughts
partialText: Amid a backlash, Gov. Josh Shapiro is pumping the brakes on enormous data centers. But in a region scarred by the collapse of the steel industry, some welcome billions in construction.

title: ‘The Nest of Snakes’: Warring Cartels Target Women in Mexico
partialText: A two-year war between rival Sinaloa Cartel factions is driving a surge in killings and disappearances targeting women.

title: John Galliano Bows Out of Met Museum Show After Criticism Mounts
partialText: Donors, politicians and Jewish leaders questioned the Met’s decision to honor Galliano, a fashion designer who was found guilty of a hate crime for his antisemitic outbursts.

title: Lionel Messi’s Retirement From Soccer Sparks Heartbreak Across Argentina
partialText: Lionel Messi’s retirement from the national soccer team, though widely expected, sparked fears of a diminished squad, and heartbreak over the departure of a national icon.

title: A Principal Saved 900 Students Before His School Was Washed Away in Nepal
partialText: Rajendra Dawadi had less than 15 minutes to act on a warning of approaching floodwaters. His swift evacuation plan saved hundreds of lives.

title: Missing in Nepal-Tibet Floods Reaches Over 4,700. Here’s What Else to Know.
partialText: The authorities in Nepal and Tibet said that more than 4,400 people were missing since a deadly Himalayan landslide and glacial collapse. Rescuers are searching for survivors.

title: This Marine Died in the Iraq War. His Mother Asks, ‘What Was It For?’
partialText: Travis Fuller was from my hometown. I went back and talked with his family about how they made sense of his death, 25 years after Sept. 11.

title: Democrats Have a Trump Card for Attacks On Wokeness
partialText: The party that capitulated to Trump has the most to answer for

title: ‘Hey! You’re the Jerk at the Beach!’
partialText: As New Yorkers, we’re used to negotiating over tiny patches of space. But I didn’t expect that to continue on the beach.

title: Death Toll Rises in Grand Canyon Flood as Search Continues
partialText: Officials announced a second death and said that more than a dozen people remain unaccounted for after heavy rain.
